title: Organelles & functions
examples: What is the main job of the mitochondria in a cell?
Can you explain the difference between the nucleus and the chloroplasts?
Where are ribosomes found inside a cell?

explain.say: Today we learn about cell organelles and what they do. Say the name of the organelle. Say its main job in the cell.

items: Mitochondria | Makes energy for the cell

explain.say: Now let me show you the real thing in 3D: an animal cell. Look at the cell membrane, the cytoplasm and the nucleus. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.
The nucleus keeps the cell's instructions safe inside. It controls what the cell does overall. Think of it like the cell's control centre.
Mitochondria are like power stations for the cell. They take food energy and release it as usable energy. This process is called respiration.
Ribosomes are tiny dots that build proteins. They read instructions from the nucleus to make things the cell needs. Protein building happens here.
Chloroplasts are found in plant cells. They use sunlight to make food through a process called photosynthesis. This gives the plant energy.
The endoplasmic reticulum and Golgi apparatus work together. The ER moves things, and the Golgi packages and sends them out.

faq.q: Why do some cells have chloroplasts and others do not?
faq.a: Chloroplasts are only found in plant cells and some algae. Animal cells do not need to make their own food using sunlight.

faq.q: Does the nucleus control everything in the cell?
faq.a: Yes, the nucleus contains the DNA, which holds the instructions for all cell activities. It directs the building of proteins and energy use.
asks: Is the nucleus the cell's brain?
What is the main job of the cell's control centre?

faq.q: What is the difference between the ER and the Golgi?
faq.a: The endoplasmic reticulum is a network that moves materials around inside the cell. The Golgi apparatus modifies and sorts these materials for sending out.
asks: What moves materials in the cell?

faq.q: Are mitochondria the same in plant and animal cells?
faq.a: Both types of cells have mitochondria because both need energy. They perform the same vital function of respiration.
asks: What do mitochondria do for all cells?

faq.q: How do ribosomes actually build proteins?
faq.a: Ribosomes read the genetic code from messenger RNA. They then link amino acids together in the correct order to form a protein chain.
asks: What is the process of protein building?

facts: The nucleus contains the cell's genetic material, or DNA.
Mitochondria are responsible for releasing energy from food during respiration.
Chloroplasts use sunlight to capture energy for food production.
Ribosomes are the sites where proteins are synthesized within the cell.

quiz.say: Which organelle is responsible for converting light energy into chemical energy?
quiz.why: Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll and are specialized for photosynthesis, which uses light energy.

wrong.0: The nucleus controls the cell but does not perform photosynthesis.
wrong.1: Ribosomes only build proteins, they do not capture light energy.
wrong.3: Mitochondria release energy from sugar, not directly from sunlight.

quiz.say: If a cell needs a lot of energy to move, which organelle would be working the hardest?
quiz.why: Mitochondria are the primary sites of cellular respiration, which generates large amounts of usable energy.

wrong.0: The ER is involved in transport, not the main energy conversion process.
wrong.2: The Golgi packages materials; it does not generate the main energy supply.
wrong.3: The nucleus stores instructions, but the mitochondria provide the power.

quiz.say: Which organelle acts like the cell's post office, modifying and sending out materials?
quiz.why: The Golgi apparatus modifies, sorts, and packages materials received from other parts of the cell for transport.

wrong.1: Chloroplasts are specialized for making food using sunlight.
wrong.2: Ribosomes are responsible only for the actual construction of protein chains.
wrong.3: Mitochondria focus on releasing chemical energy from food sources.
